h: Exeter climbing, from booking to brew
p: Got a mixed bag of ages? Clip 'n Climb is one of the few activities where a primary schooler and a grown-up can genuinely do the same thing side by side, and the kid quite often wins. Still, it's worth checking the age guidance when you book, as there's usually a minimum age for climbers and some rules on supervising younger children.

Every climber needs a participation form filling in, signed by a parent or guardian for under-18s, so do that online before you set off. Allow a couple of hours for the whole visit, and arrive a little early so harness fitting and the safety briefing don't eat into your time on the walls.

A couple of climbing pointers. Push with your legs rather than hauling with your arms, and you'll last much longer. On the side-by-side race walls, a steady climber often beats a frantic one. And on the jump challenges, look at your target, not the floor.

Afterwards, the Royal Albert Memorial Museum, known locally as RAMM, is free and full of surprises, from natural history to world cultures. The Exeter Ship Canal runs from the Quay down towards Topsham and the estuary, a flat route for a walk or bike ride, and Topsham itself is a pretty little riverside town for a bite to eat. If you'd rather head into the trees, Haldon Forest Park sits on the ridge just outside the city with trails for all abilities.
